title.en: The Relationship Between Parents and Children

title.ar: الدَّرْسُ الأَوَّل: العَلاقَةُ بَينَ الآباءِ وَالأَبْناء
title.en: Lesson 1: The relationship between parents and children (reading)
title.ur: Sabaq 1: Walidain aur aulad ka rishta (parhna)

intro.en: In this reading the Quran sets the limits of the relationship between parents and children. We meet Luqman advising his son, Ibrahim and Ismail, and Nuh and his son.
intro.ur: Is parhne ke sabaq mein Quran walidain aur aulad ke rishte ki hudood batata hai. Hum Luqman ka apne bete ko nasihat karna, Ibrahim aur Ismail, aur Nuh aur unke bete ka zikr parhenge.
intro.ar: في هذِهِ القِراءَةِ يَرْسُمُ القُرْآنُ حُدودَ العَلاقَةِ بَيْنَ الآباءِ وَالأَبْناءِ. نَتَعَرَّفُ نُصْحَ لُقْمانَ لِابْنِهِ، وَإِبْراهيمَ وَإِسْماعيلَ، وَنُوحاً وَابْنَهُ.

dialogue.ar: تَحْتاجُ كُلُّ أُسْرَةٍ إِلى عَلاقَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ بَيْنَ الآباءِ وَالأَبْناءِ، وَهذِهِ قَضِيَّةٌ تَهُمُّ الجَميعَ.
dialogue.tr: taḥtāju kullu usratin ilā ʿalāqatin ṭayyibatin bayna l-ābāʾi wa-l-abnāʾ, wa-hādhihi qaḍiyyatun tahummu l-jamīʿ
dialogue.en: Every family needs a good relationship between parents and children, and this is a matter that concerns everyone.
dialogue.ur: Har khandan ko walidain aur aulad ke darmiyan achhe rishte ki zaroorat hoti hai, aur yeh aisa mas'ala hai jo sab ko ahem hai.

dialogue.ar: وَقَدْ ذَكَرَ القُرْآنُ الكَريمُ قِصَصاً لِنَتَعَلَّمَ مِنْها كَيْفَ يَكونُ الأَبُ وَكَيْفَ يَكونُ الابْنُ.
dialogue.tr: wa-qad dhakara l-qurʾānu l-karīmu qiṣaṣan li-nataʿallama minhā kayfa yakūnu l-abu wa-kayfa yakūnu l-ibn
dialogue.en: The Noble Quran mentioned stories so that we learn from them what a father should be and what a son should be.
dialogue.ur: Quran-e-Kareem ne kuch qisse bayan kiye taake hum seekhein ke baap kaisa ho aur beta kaisa ho.

dialogue.ar: فَلُقْمانُ الحَكيمُ أَبٌ يُحِبُّ ابْنَهُ، فَيَبْدَأُ بِتَعْليمِهِ أَهَمَّ شَيْءٍ: أَنْ يَعْبُدَ اللهَ وَحْدَهُ.
dialogue.tr: fa-luqmānu l-ḥakīmu abun yuḥibbu ibnahu, fa-yabdaʾu bi-taʿlīmihi ahamma shayʾin: an yaʿbuda llāha waḥdah
dialogue.en: Luqman the Wise is a father who loves his son, so he begins by teaching him the most important thing: to worship Allah alone.
dialogue.ur: Luqman Hakeem aisa baap hai jo apne bete se mohabbat karta hai, isliye sab se ahem baat se shuru karta hai: sirf Allah ki ibadat.

dialogue.ar: قالَ لُقْمانُ لِابْنِهِ: ﴿يَا بُنَيَّ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ  إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾
dialogue.tr: qāla luqmānu li-bnihi: yā bunayya lā tushrik billāhi inna sh-shirka la-ẓulmun ʿaẓīm
dialogue.en: Luqman said to his son: «O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, shirk is a great wrong.»
dialogue.ur: Luqman ne apne bete se kaha: "Ae mere bete, Allah ke saath kisi ko shareek na thehrana. Beshak shirk bada zulm hai."

dialogue.ar: ثُمَّ عَلَّمَهُ أَنَّ اللهَ يَرى أَقْوالَهُ وَأَعْمالَهُ، فَعَلَيْهِ مُراقَبَتُهُ في كُلِّ ما يَفْعَلُ.
dialogue.tr: thumma ʿallamahu anna llāha yarā aqwālahu wa-aʿmālah, fa-ʿalayhi murāqabatuhu fī kulli mā yafʿal
dialogue.en: Then he taught him that Allah sees his words and deeds, so he should be mindful of Him in all he does.
dialogue.ur: Phir usay sikhaya ke Allah uski baatein aur kaam dekhta hai, isliye jo bhi kare us mein Allah ko yaad rakhe.

dialogue.ar: وَعَلَّمَهُ أَنْ يَكونَ مُتَواضِعاً لا مُتَكَبِّراً، وَأَنْ يَسيرَ بِهُدوءٍ وَيَتَكَلَّمَ بِصَوْتٍ مُنْخَفِضٍ.
dialogue.tr: wa-ʿallamahu an yakūna mutawāḍiʿan lā mutakabbiran, wa-an yasīra bi-hudūʾin wa-yatakallama bi-ṣawtin munkhafiḍ
dialogue.en: He taught him to be humble, not proud, to walk calmly and speak in a low voice.
dialogue.ur: Usay sikhaya ke inkisar wala ho, mutakabbir nahin, sukoon se chale aur dheemi aawaz mein baat kare.

dialogue.ar: ﴿وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ وَاغْضُضْ مِن صَوْتِكَ﴾
dialogue.tr: waqṣid fī mashyika waghḍuḍ min ṣawtik
dialogue.en: «Be moderate in your walk and lower your voice.»
dialogue.ur: "Apni chaal mein miyana-rawi rakho aur apni aawaz past rakho."

dialogue.ar: وَإِذا كانَ لُقْمانُ مِثالاً لِلأُبُوَّةِ الحَكيمَةِ، فَإِسْماعيلُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ مِثالٌ لِلبُنُوَّةِ البارَّةِ.
dialogue.tr: wa-idhā kāna luqmānu mithālan li-l-ubuwwati l-ḥakīma, fa-ismāʿīlu ʿalayhi s-salāmu mithālun li-l-bunuwwati l-bārra
dialogue.en: If Luqman is an example of wise fatherhood, Ismail, peace be upon him, is an example of dutiful sonhood.
dialogue.ur: Agar Luqman hikmat bhari ubuwwat ki misaal hain to Ismail alaihis-salam farmanbardar bete ki misaal hain.

dialogue.ar: فَحينَ أَخْبَرَهُ أَبوهُ إِبْراهيمُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ بِما أُمِرَ بِهِ، لَمْ يَعْتَرِضْ، بَلْ قالَ:
dialogue.tr: fa-ḥīna akhbarahu abūhu ibrāhīmu ʿalayhi s-salāmu bi-mā umira bih, lam yaʿtariḍ, bal qāl
dialogue.en: When his father Ibrahim, peace be upon him, told him what he had been commanded, he did not object but said:
dialogue.ur: Jab unke walid Ibrahim alaihis-salam ne unhein us hukm se aagah kiya jo unhein mila tha, to unhon ne etiraz nahin kiya balkay kaha:

dialogue.ar: ﴿يَا أَبَتِ افْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ  سَتَجِدُنِي إِن شَاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾
dialogue.tr: yā abati fʿal mā tuʾmar satajidunī in shāʾa llāhu mina ṣ-ṣābirīn
dialogue.en: «O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient.»
dialogue.ur: "Abbajaan, jo aapko hukm diya gaya hai woh kar dijiye. Insha-Allah aap mujhe sabr karne walon mein payenge."

dialogue.ar: وَأَمّا نُوحٌ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ فَدَعا ابْنَهُ بِعَطْفٍ، وَلكِنَّ الابْنَ اخْتارَ طَريقاً آخَرَ.
dialogue.tr: wa-ammā nūḥun ʿalayhi s-salāmu fa-daʿā ibnahu bi-ʿaṭfin, wa-lākinna l-ibna khtāra ṭarīqan ākhar
dialogue.en: As for Nuh, peace be upon him, he called his son tenderly, but the son chose another path.
dialogue.ur: Rahe Nuh alaihis-salam, to unhon ne apne bete ko shafqat se pukara, lekin bete ne doosra raasta chuna.

dialogue.ar: وَهكَذا نَفْهَمُ أَنَّ لِلآباءِ واجِباً في النُّصْحِ وَالتَّرْبِيَةِ، وَلِلأَبْناءِ واجِباً في البِرِّ وَالطّاعَةِ بِالمَعْروفِ.
dialogue.tr: wa-hākadhā nafhamu anna li-l-ābāʾi wājiban fī n-nuṣḥi wa-t-tarbiya, wa-li-l-abnāʾi wājiban fī l-birri wa-ṭ-ṭāʿati bi-l-maʿrūf
dialogue.en: So we understand that parents have a duty of advice and upbringing, and children have a duty of kindness and obedience in what is right.
dialogue.ur: Is tarah hum samajhte hain ke walidain ka farz nasihat aur tarbiyat hai, aur aulad ka farz neki aur maroof mein itaat hai.

q.en: Who is called the wise father who advised his son?
q.ur: Kis ko Hakeem baap kaha gaya jisne bete ko nasihat ki?
q.ar: مَنِ الأَبُ الحَكيمُ الَّذي نَصَحَ ابْنَهُ؟

q.en: What was the first thing Luqman gave his son?
q.ur: Luqman ne bete ko sab se pehle kya diya?
q.ar: ما أَوَّلُ ما قَدَّمَهُ لُقْمانُ لِابْنِهِ؟

q.en: Who gave a high example in sonhood (البُنُوَّة)?
q.ur: Beta hone ki behtareen misaal kis ne di?
q.ar: مَنْ ضَرَبَ مَثَلاً عالِياً في البُنُوَّةِ؟

intro.en: Here we practise the reading: match words, find meanings and answer short questions about the story of Luqman, Ibrahim, Ismail and Nuh.
intro.ur: Yahan hum matan ki mashq karte hain: lafzon ko milana, matlab dhoondhna aur Luqman, Ibrahim, Ismail aur Nuh ke qisse par chhote sawalon ke jawab dena.
intro.ar: نَتَدَرَّبُ عَلى النَّصِّ: نُطابِقُ الكَلِماتِ، وَنَجِدُ المَعاني، وَنُجيبُ عَنْ أَسْئِلَةٍ قَصيرَةٍ حَوْلَ قِصَّةِ لُقْمانَ وَإِبْراهيمَ وَإِسْماعيلَ وَنُوحٍ.

dialogue.ar: ماذا كانَ أَوَّلَ ما عَلَّمَهُ لُقْمانُ لِابْنِهِ؟
dialogue.tr: mādhā kāna awwala mā ʿallamahu luqmānu li-bnih?
dialogue.en: What was the first thing Luqman taught his son?
dialogue.ur: Luqman ne apne bete ko sab se pehle kya sikhaya?

dialogue.ar: كَيْفَ أَوْصى لُقْمانُ ابْنَهُ أَنْ يَمْشِيَ وَيَتَكَلَّمَ؟
dialogue.tr: kayfa awṣā luqmānu ibnahu an yamshiya wa-yatakallam?
dialogue.en: How did Luqman advise his son to walk and to speak?
dialogue.ur: Luqman ne bete ko chalne aur bolne ke baare mein kya wasiyyat ki?

dialogue.ar: لِماذا كانَ إِسْماعيلُ مِثالاً لِلْبُنُوَّةِ البارَّةِ؟
dialogue.tr: li-mādhā kāna ismāʿīlu mithālan li-l-bunuwwati l-bārra?
dialogue.en: Why was Ismail an example of dutiful sonhood?
dialogue.ur: Ismail dutiful beta hone ki misaal kyun hain?

dialogue.ar: ما واجِبُ الآباءِ وَما واجِبُ الأَبْناءِ؟
dialogue.tr: mā wājibu l-ābāʾi wa-mā wājibu l-abnāʾ?
dialogue.en: What is the duty of parents and what is the duty of children?
dialogue.ur: Walidain ka farz kya hai aur aulad ka farz kya hai?

vocab.en: to disown, to declare oneself free of

q.en: What does the Quran say people should cooperate on?
q.ur: Quran ke mutabiq log kis par aapas mein madad karen?
q.ar: عَلى ماذا يَأْمُرُنا القُرْآنُ أَنْ نَتَعاوَنَ؟

title.en: Lesson 3: Grammar (a): The nun of protection (نون الوقاية)

intro.en: When a verb or a word like إِنَّ, لَيْتَ, لَعَلَّ is followed by 'me' (ي), a protective ن comes in between: يُطْعِمُني (he feeds me), إِنَّني (indeed I). It protects the end of the verb from a kasra. Example: أُمّي تَسْقيني الحَليبَ، وَلكِنَّني أُحِبُّ العَصيرَ.
intro.ur: Jab kisi fail ya إِنَّ، لَيْتَ، لَعَلَّ ke baad 'mujhe/mera' (ي) aaye to beech mein ek ن aata hai jise Noon-ul-Wiqaya kehte hain: يُطْعِمُني (woh mujhe khilata hai), إِنَّني (beshak main). Yeh fail ke aakhir ko kasra se bachata hai. Misaal: أُمّي تَسْقيني الحَليبَ، وَلكِنَّني أُحِبُّ العَصيرَ (ammi mujhe doodh pilati hain, lekin mujhe juice pasand hai).
intro.ar: إِذا جاءَتْ ياءُ المُتَكَلِّمِ بَعْدَ فِعْلٍ أَوْ بَعْدَ «إِنَّ» وَ«لَيْتَ» وَ«لَعَلَّ» تَدْخُلُ نونٌ تَحْمي آخِرَها مِنَ الكَسْرِ، وَتُسَمّى نُونَ الوِقايَةِ، مِثْلُ: يُطْعِمُني، إِنَّني. وَمِثالٌ: أُمّي تَسْقيني الحَليبَ، وَلكِنَّني أُحِبُّ العَصيرَ.

dialogue.ar: الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ
dialogue.tr: alladhī khalaqanī fa-huwa yahdīn
dialogue.en: The One who created me, so He guides me.
dialogue.ur: Jis ne mujhe paida kiya, wohi mujhe hidayat deta hai.

dialogue.ar: إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي
dialogue.tr: innanī anā llāhu lā ilāha illā anā fa-ʿbudnī
dialogue.en: Indeed I am Allah, there is no god but Me, so worship Me.
dialogue.ur: Beshak main hi Allah hoon, mere siwa koi mabood nahin, pas meri ibadat karo.

dialogue.ar: لَّعَلِّي أَبْلُغُ الْأَسْبَابَ
dialogue.tr: laʿallī ablughu l-asbāb
dialogue.en: Perhaps I may reach the ways.
dialogue.ur: Shayad main raaste (asbaab) tak pahunch jaaun.

dialogue.ar: رَأَيْتُ كَأَنَّني في دِرْعٍ حَصينَةٍ
dialogue.tr: raʾaytu ka-annanī fī dirʿin ḥaṣīna
dialogue.en: I saw as if I were in a strong coat of armour.
dialogue.ur: Maine dekha goya main ek mazboot zirah mein hoon.

dialogue.ar: أُمّي تَسْقيني الحَليبَ كُلَّ صَباحٍ، وَلكِنَّني أُحِبُّ العَصيرَ.
dialogue.tr: ummī tasqīnī l-ḥalība kulla ṣabāḥ, wa-lākinnanī uḥibbu l-ʿaṣīr
dialogue.en: My mother gives me milk every morning, but I like juice.
dialogue.ur: Ammi mujhe har subah doodh pilati hain, lekin mujhe juice pasand hai.

dialogue.ar: لَيْتَني أَسْتَطيعُ أَنْ أُساعِدَكَ يا صَديقي.
dialogue.tr: laytanī astaṭīʿu an usāʿidaka yā ṣadīqī
dialogue.en: If only I could help you, my friend.
dialogue.ur: Kaash main aapki madad kar sakta, mere dost.

q.en: What is the job of the nun of protection?

options: It protects the verb's ending before ي (me)
options_ar: حِمايَةُ آخِرِ الفِعْلِ قَبْلَ ياءِ المُتَكَلِّمِ

q.ur: 'Beshak main' ke liye durust lafz kaun sa hai?
q.ar: أَيُّ كِتابَةٍ صَحيحَةٌ لِـ «إِنَّ» مَعَ ياءِ المُتَكَلِّمِ؟

title.en: Lesson 4: Listening: The family and children's friends
title.ur: Sabaq 4: Sun kar samajhna: Khandaan aur bachon ke dost

intro.en: Listen and answer: why parents think about their children's friends, and what a family does when a friend is a bad influence. Friends affect each other, so families care about them.
intro.ur: Suno aur jawab do: walidain bachon ke doston ke baare mein kyun sochte hain, aur agar dost bura ho to khandaan kya karta hai. Dost ek doosre par asar daalte hain, isliye ghar wale unki fikr karte hain.
intro.ar: نَسْتَمِعُ وَنُجيبُ: لِماذا يَهْتَمُّ الوالِدانِ بِأَصْدِقاءِ أَبْنائِهِما؟ وَماذا تَفْعَلُ الأُسْرَةُ إِذا كانَ الصَّديقُ سَيِّئَ التَّأْثيرِ؟ فَالأَصْدِقاءُ يُؤَثِّرونَ في بَعْضِهِمْ.

dialogue.ar: لِماذا يَسْأَلُ الأَبُ عَنْ أَصْحابِ ابْنِهِ؟
dialogue.tr: li-mādhā yasʾalu l-abu ʿan aṣḥābi ibnih?
dialogue.en: Why does the father ask about his son's companions?
dialogue.ur: Baap apne bete ke saathiyon ke baare mein kyun poochta hai?

dialogue.ar: لِأَنَّ الأَصْدِقاءَ يَتَعَلَّمونَ مِنْ عاداتِ بَعْضِهِمْ.
dialogue.tr: li-anna l-aṣdiqāʾa yataʿallamūna min ʿādāti baʿḍihim
dialogue.en: Because friends learn from each other's habits.
dialogue.ur: Kyunke dost ek doosre ki aadatein seekhte hain.

dialogue.ar: كَيْفَ تَتَعَرَّفُ الأُسْرَةُ إِلى أَصْدِقاءِ أَبْنائِها؟
dialogue.tr: kayfa tataʿarrafu l-usratu ilā aṣdiqāʾi abnāʾihā?
dialogue.en: How does the family get to know its children's friends?
dialogue.ur: Khandan apne bachon ke doston se kaise waqif hota hai?

dialogue.ar: تَدْعوهُمْ إِلى زِيارَةِ البَيْتِ وَتَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَهُمْ.
dialogue.tr: tadʿūhum ilā ziyārati l-bayti wa-tataḥaddathu maʿahum
dialogue.en: It invites them to visit the home and talks with them.
dialogue.ur: Unhein ghar aane ki dawat deta hai aur unse baat karta hai.

q.en: Why do parents ask about their children's friends?
q.ur: Walidain bachon ke doston ke baare mein kyun poochte hain?
q.ar: لِماذا يَسْأَلُ الوالِدانِ عَنْ أَصْدِقاءِ أَبْنائِهِما؟

options: Because friends learn from each other's habits
options_ar: لِأَنَّ الأَصْدِقاءَ يَتَعَلَّمونَ مِنْ عاداتِ بَعْضِهِمْ

q.en: How does the family get to know the children's friends?
q.ur: Ghar wale bachon ke doston se kaise waqif hote hain?
q.ar: كَيْفَ تَتَعَرَّفُ الأُسْرَةُ إِلى أَصْدِقاءِ الأَوْلادِ؟

options: By inviting them to visit the home

title.en: Lesson 5: Speaking and writing: The dutiful child
title.ur: Sabaq 5: Bolna aur likhna: Farmanbardar bacha

intro.en: Ask and answer questions with a partner about treating parents well, then write a story called 'A child dutiful to his parents'.
intro.ur: Apne saathi ke saath walidain se acha sulook karne ke baare mein sawal jawab karein, phir 'Walidain ka farmanbardar bacha' ke unwan par kahani likhein.
intro.ar: نَسْأَلُ وَنُجيبُ مَعَ زَميلٍ عَنِ الإِحْسانِ إِلى الوالِدَيْنِ، ثُمَّ نَكْتُبُ قِصَّةً بِعُنْوانِ «الوَلَدُ البارُّ بِوالِدَيْهِ».

dialogue.ar: ماذا تَفْعَلُ لِتُسْعِدَ أُمَّكَ وَأَباكَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ؟
dialogue.tr: mādhā tafʿalu li-tusʿida ummaka wa-abāka kulla yawm?
dialogue.en: What do you do to make your mother and father happy every day?
dialogue.ur: Aap har roz apni ammi aur abbu ko khush karne ke liye kya karte hain?

dialogue.ar: لِماذا نُحْسِنُ إِلى والِدَيْنا حينَ يَكْبَرانِ؟
dialogue.tr: li-mādhā nuḥsinu ilā wālidaynā ḥīna yakbarān?
dialogue.en: Why do we do good to our parents when they grow old?
dialogue.ur: Jab walidain boorhe ho jayen to hum unke saath ehsaan kyun karein?

dialogue.ar: ماذا يَنالُ الابْنُ البارُّ جَزاءً لِإِحْسانِهِ؟
dialogue.tr: mādhā yanālu l-ibnu l-bārru jazāʾan li-iḥsānih?
dialogue.en: What does a dutiful child receive as a reward for his kindness?
dialogue.ur: Farmanbardar beta apni neki ke badle mein kya paata hai?

dialogue.ar: هَلْ تَسْتَمِعُ إِلى نَصائِحِ أُسْرَتِكَ؟ مَتى تُفيدُكَ؟
dialogue.tr: hal tastamiʿu ilā naṣāʾiḥi usratik? matā tufīduk?
dialogue.en: Do you listen to your family's advice? When does it help you?
dialogue.ur: Kya aap apne ghar walon ki nasihatein sunte hain? Woh aapko kab faida deti hain?

dialogue.ar: البِرُّ بِالوالِدَيْنِ طَريقٌ إِلى رِضا اللهِ.
dialogue.tr: al-birru bi-l-wālidayni ṭarīqun ilā riḍā llāh
dialogue.en: Kindness to one's parents is a path to Allah's pleasure.
dialogue.ur: Walidain ke saath neki Allah ki raza ka raasta hai.

options_ar: ما يُعْطى مُقابِلَ العَمَلِ ثَواباً أَوْ عِقاباً

q.en: According to the sentence, kindness to parents is a path to...
q.ur: Jumle ke mutabiq walidain ke saath neki kis ka raasta hai?
q.ar: بِحَسَبِ الجُمْلَةِ، البِرُّ بِالوالِدَيْنِ طَريقٌ إِلى...

title.en: Lesson 6: Spelling: joining and separating مَنْ
title.ur: Sabaq 6: Imla: «مَنْ» ka milna aur alag likhna

intro.en: Rule: when a preposition comes before مَنْ, they join and the ن doubles: عَمَّنْ, مِمَّنْ, فِيمَنْ. When مَنْ comes first and the preposition after it, they stay separate: مَنْ في المَكْتَبَةِ؟
intro.ur: Qaida: agar harf-e-jar مَنْ se pehle aaye to dono mil jate hain: عَمَّنْ، مِمَّنْ، فِيمَنْ. Agar مَنْ pehle aaye aur harf-e-jar baad mein to alag likhte hain: مَنْ في المَكْتَبَةِ؟
intro.ar: القاعِدَةُ: إِذا سَبَقَ حَرْفُ الجَرِّ «مَنْ» اتَّصَلا وَشُدِّدَتِ النّونُ: عَمَّنْ، مِمَّنْ، فِيمَنْ. وَإِذا جاءَتْ «مَنْ» أَوَّلاً ثُمَّ حَرْفُ الجَرِّ بَقِيا مُنْفَصِلَيْنِ: مَنْ في المَكْتَبَةِ؟

dialogue.ar: عَمَّنْ تَتَحَدَّثُ؟
dialogue.tr: ʿamman tataḥaddath?
dialogue.en: Whom are you talking about?
dialogue.ur: Aap kis ke baare mein baat kar rahe hain?

dialogue.ar: مِمَّنِ اشْتَرَيْتَ الكِتابَ؟
dialogue.tr: mimmani shtarayta l-kitāb?
dialogue.en: From whom did you buy the book?
dialogue.ur: Aapne kitab kis se kharidi?

dialogue.ar: فِيمَنْ تُفَكِّرُ؟
dialogue.tr: fīman tufakkir?
dialogue.en: Whom are you thinking of?
dialogue.ur: Aap kis ke baare mein soch rahe hain?

dialogue.ar: مَنْ مِنَ الأَوْلادِ فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ؟
dialogue.tr: man mina l-awlādi fahima d-dars?
dialogue.en: Which of the boys understood the lesson?
dialogue.ur: Larkon mein se kis ne sabaq samjha?

dialogue.ar: مَنْ في المَكْتَبَةِ الآنَ؟
dialogue.tr: man fī l-maktabati l-ān?
dialogue.en: Who is in the library now?
dialogue.ur: Is waqt library mein kaun hai?

q.en: When a preposition comes before مَنْ, they...
q.ur: Harf-e-jar مَنْ se pehle aaye to...
Kaun sa milakar likha jata hai?
q.ar: أَيُّ عِبارَةٍ كُتِبَتْ فيها الكَلِمَتانِ مُتَّصِلَتَيْنِ؟

q.en: When مَنْ comes first, then a preposition, they are...
q.ur: Jab مَنْ pehle ho aur harf-e-jar baad mein to...
q.ar: إِذا جاءَتْ «مَنْ» أَوَّلاً ثُمَّ حَرْفُ الجَرِّ فَإِنَّهُما...

title.en: Lesson 7: Grammar (b): Verbal nouns of three-letter verbs
title.ur: Sabaq 7: Qawaid (be): Teen harfi afaal ke masdar

intro.en: The masdar (verbal noun) means an action without time, like 'travelling'. Many three-letter masdars are learned by hearing, but some patterns are common: فَعيل for sounds animals make (صَهَلَ: صَهيلاً), فُعال for body sounds and illness (عَطَسَ: عُطاساً), فِعالَة for a craft (نَجَرَ: نِجارَةً), فُعْلَة for colour (زَرِقَ: زُرْقَةً), فَعَلان for movement (دارَ: دَوَراناً).
intro.ur: Masdar wo lafz hai jo bina zamane ke kaam ka matlab de, jaise 'safar karna'. Bohat se teen harfi masdar sun kar yaad hote hain, lekin kuch wazan aam hain: فَعيل jaanwaron ki aawaz ke liye (صَهَلَ: صَهيلاً)، فُعال jism ki aawaz aur bimari ke liye (عَطَسَ: عُطاساً)، فِعالَة pesha ke liye (نَجَرَ: نِجارَةً)، فُعْلَة rang ke liye (زَرِقَ: زُرْقَةً)، فَعَلان harkat ke liye (دارَ: دَوَراناً).
intro.ar: المَصْدَرُ اسْمٌ يَدُلُّ عَلى الحَدَثِ مِنْ غَيْرِ زَمَنٍ، مِثْلُ «السَّفَرِ». وَأَكْثَرُ مَصادِرِ الثُّلاثِيِّ سَماعِيَّةٌ، وَمِنْها أَوْزانٌ شائِعَةٌ: فَعيل لِأَصْواتِ الحَيَوانِ (صَهَلَ: صَهيلاً)، وَفُعال لِأَصْواتِ الجِسْمِ وَالمَرَضِ (عَطَسَ: عُطاساً)، وَفِعالَة لِلحِرْفَةِ (نَجَرَ: نِجارَةً)، وَفُعْلَة لِلَّوْنِ (زَرِقَ: زُرْقَةً)، وَفَعَلان لِلحَرَكَةِ (دارَ: دَوَراناً).

dialogue.ar: صَهَلَ: صَهيلاً
dialogue.tr: ṣahala: ṣahīlan
dialogue.en: to neigh: neighing
dialogue.ur: hinhinana: hinhinahat

dialogue.ar: عَطَسَ: عُطاساً
dialogue.tr: ʿaṭasa: ʿuṭāsan
dialogue.en: to sneeze: a sneeze
dialogue.ur: chheenkna: chheenk

dialogue.ar: صَرَخَ: صُراخاً
dialogue.tr: ṣarakha: ṣurākhan
dialogue.en: to shout: shouting
dialogue.ur: cheekhna: cheekh

dialogue.ar: نَجَرَ: نِجارَةً
dialogue.tr: najara: nijāratan
dialogue.en: to carve wood: carpentry
dialogue.ur: lakdi tarashna: barhai ka kaam

dialogue.ar: زَرِقَ: زُرْقَةً
dialogue.tr: zariqa: zurqatan
dialogue.en: to be blue: blueness
dialogue.ur: neela hona: neelahat

dialogue.ar: دارَ: دَوَراناً
dialogue.tr: dāra: dawarānan
dialogue.en: to turn: turning
dialogue.ur: ghoomna: gardish

dialogue.ar: خَفَقَ: خَفَقاناً
dialogue.tr: khafaqa: khafaqānan
dialogue.en: to beat (heart): beating
dialogue.ur: dhadakna: dhadkan

q.en: The masdar of رَحَلَ (to depart) is...
q.ur: رَحَلَ ka masdar kaun sa hai?

q.en: The pattern فِعالَة is used for...
q.ur: Wazan فِعالَة kis ke liye hai?

q.en: The masdar of غَلى (to boil) is...
The pattern فُعْلَة is used for...
q.ur: Wazan فُعْلَة kis ke liye hai?
